text: Input lets you read text from the user, pausing the program for their response.
Input always returns a string, [chuckle] even if they type a number.
Convert it with int or float if you need to do math.
The text you pass to input becomes the prompt shown on screen, so the user knows what to type.
Then print the results using f-strings for clean output.
Print takes extra keyword arguments too — sep changes the separator between values, and end controls what comes after, instead of a newline.
[sniff] F-strings support formatting mini-language — colon f dot two rounds a price to two decimal places.
[groan] F-strings can run real expressions inside the braces too, like doing math right in the middle of your text.
And the greater-than or less-than symbols control alignment and padding width, [groan] handy for lining up columns.
Always wrap user input conversion in a try block — [laugh] you can never fully trust what someone types in.
